summary: Tarball contains double-percent-encoded path-traversal entries writing outside the package root
details: The npm tarball ships directory entries whose names are double-URL-encoded `..` sequences (`%252e%252e/%252e%252e/%252e%252e/tmp/npm-traversal-double_percent`) terminating in a file dropped at `/tmp/npm-traversal-double_percent` outside the package's own install directory. On a tar extractor that single-decodes percent-encoding before applying path-safety checks, extraction of this archive writes attacker-chosen files to absolute filesystem paths on the installer host during `npm install`. The shipped JavaScript is an inert stub and no lifecycle scripts are declared; the attack surface is the archive layout itself, exercised by the package manager's extraction step. Package naming (`@h1stealthy/...-transfer-...`) and the marker payload are consistent with a controlled traversal probe, but the artifact as published is structurally a path-traversal (zip-slip-style) tar against npm clients.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
